title: [Performance] Use direct transpose batch matmul for V up projection
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

SFA V up-projection now always uses `npu_transpose_batchmatmul` with `perm_x1=(1, 0, 2)` when the fused operator is available. The old `N * L >= 65536` branch made an explicit transpose and contiguous copy. CANN 9.2.0-beta.2 accepts the direct call at and above that boundary.

Measured on Ascend 910B4 with BF16, using the full `_v_up_proj` path and synchronizing after each call (60 interleaved measurements, median):

| B, N, L, V | N * L | Previous | Direct |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16, 32, 512, 128 | 16,384 | 133.5 us | 133.0 us |
| 16, 128, 512, 128 | 65,536 | 191.3 us | 135.6 us |
| 16, 128, 768, 128 | 98,304 | 191.2 us | 137.6 us |

The `torch.bmm` fallback remains available when the fused operator is absent. The direct large-shape path depends on a CANN build supporting `N * L >= 65536`; it was verified with 9.2.0-beta.2.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. SFA V up-projection latency improves for large `N * L`; output shape and API stay the same.

### How was this patch tested?

- Called the patched `AscendSFAImpl._v_up_proj` on Ascend 910B4 / CANN 9.2.0-beta.2 for BF16 and FP16 at `N * L = 32768, 65536, 98304`, comparing every output element against FP32 `torch.bmm`. All 6 cases passed; maximum absolute error was 0.00383 (BF16) and 0.000457 (FP16).
- Before the patch, compared both fused layouts against FP32 `torch.bmm` over 7 shapes, 2 dtypes, and 3 seeds (42 cases); all passed. Additional BF16 checks passed at `N * L = 131072, 262144, 524288`.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `git diff --check` passed. `bash format.sh ci` could not start because `pre-commit` is not installed in this environment.
- No repository test was added; validation used direct NPU measurements of the operator and the patched method. The standard unit-test invocation in this workspace cannot load `tests/ut/conftest.py` because its vLLM checkout lacks `prepare_dcp_local_seq_lens`.

---
